blockers: The canonical silhouette still reads as a narrow, symmetrical mannequin: a rounded blue torso, rectangular pelvis, parallel stick-like legs, and two outward arm blobs. The rapier supplies most of the silhouette identity; the body itself does not communicate a distinctive controlled fencer.

The visual proportions do not convincingly achieve the stated 5.5-head design. The head is undersized against the approximately 116px total height, while the legs dominate the figure, producing an elongated doll-like ratio rather than deliberate vertical elegance.

At native 1x, navy torso shadows, black collar and hair, dark boots, and blue lower-body planes collapse into weak internal separation. Brass accents are reduced to tiny yellow pixels, and the thin rapier loses authority against the light-background inspection.

The face is not structurally readable at native scale. The features collapse into a pale horizontal strip with insufficient eye spacing, nose definition, jaw shape, or expression, while the hair reads as a featureless dark cap. This creates a mannequin-like result rather than a stylized face.

The locomotion keys show pendulum-like limb swings beneath an almost locked vertical torso. There is little visible compression, pelvis translation, hip/shoulder counter-rotation, or convincing passing and recovery phase. The diagonal rows look like view variants of the same rig rather than authored 8-direction locomotion.

Foot contact is technically anchored but visually ambiguous. The boots are too thin to establish a clear sole, heel, or toe, and planted and lifted feet are not sufficiently differentiated. The cycle therefore risks reading as sliding even though the measured anchor drift is zero.

The signature gesture does not establish a strong anticipation, decisive action silhouette, overshoot, and settle. The rapier changes angle, but the torso, center of mass, feet, and sword-side shoulder contribute too little, so the motion reads as weapon jitter rather than a character-specific Celina action.

Secondary motion is effectively absent. Hair, collar, brass elements, limbs, and rapier appear rigidly coupled, with no delayed tip follow-through or controlled settle to sell restraint and material hierarchy.
high_value_changes: Redesign one canonical front and side pose at native 1x before propagating the animation: enlarge and structurally simplify the face, taper the corset into a more deliberate waist and pelvis, separate the thigh/knee/boot planes, and replace the symmetric arm blobs with a clear sword-side asymmetry.

Increase value separation between collar, hair, torso, corset, thigh armor, boots, and brass. Give the rapier a stronger readable shaft and guard treatment that survives both dark and light backgrounds without relying on a fragile single-pixel line.

Rebuild the walk cycle from explicit contact, down, passing, and up keys. Add a visible weight-bearing hip, knee compression, heel-to-toe roll, torso counter-rotation, and shoulder response; author diagonal depth and occlusion independently instead of interpolating from side poses.

Re-author the gesture as a controlled fencing action with a readable anticipation pose, clear rapier-led primary action, a held endpoint, tip overshoot, and delayed settle in the wrist, collar, and hair. The final pose must be identifiable from the silhouette alone.

Add restrained but measurable secondary motion: rapier-tip follow-through, collar or hair lag, brass accent response, and a short settle after the main action. The motion should remain deliberate without becoming static.
Use a native-1x facial design pass with fewer, higher-value features rather than tiny 3D facial detail. Establish clear eye spacing, a readable jaw/neck transition, and one controlled expression.
optional_notes: The measured 0.0px anchor drift and sub-128px standing height are compliant, but technical compliance does not compensate for weak visual foot contact or native-scale readability.
The static sheet reports 116.0px while the evaluation context reports 115.6px. Both values are compliant, but the production measurement source should be unified.
The supplied strips account for 16 idle plus 64 locomotion plus 24 gesture frames, totaling 104, while the context reports 105 rendered frames. Reconcile the frame accounting before final export.
regressions_from_previous: No round-12 imagery, metrics, or comparison sheet was supplied, so visual regressions from the previous iteration cannot be verified.
strongest_improvements: The rapier, high collar, brass shoulder details, and midnight-blue palette establish a basic fencing identity hook, although they currently carry more identity than the body design can support.
The reported ground anchor is stable at 0.0px drift.
The candidate includes the complete stated 8-direction and signature-gesture frame coverage, but coverage alone does not establish readable motion quality.
luna_evaluation.single_most_important_next_change: Rebuild the canonical silhouette at native 1x around a clearly weight-bearing, asymmetrical fencer stance with a larger readable face, tapered corset, separated legs and boots, and a stronger rapier-side gesture; do not revise the full animation set until this base pose reads unmistakably without magnification.
